---
title: "Branch protection"
description: "The ruleset settings the workflows rely on."
---

The workflows work without branch protection, but the branch model only
holds if GitHub enforces it. These are the settings the workflows expect,
configured as [repository or organization rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets).

## `dev`

- **Require a pull request before merging.**
- **Require status checks to pass**: the jobs of [R CMD check](r-cmd-check.qmd)
  and [Commitlint](commitlint.qmd), plus any others you rely on.
- Block force pushes and deletion.

Suggestion PRs target your feature branches, not `dev`, so they are not
affected. The monthly [sweep](suggestions.qmd#sweeps) PR does target `dev`;
with the [GitHub App](getting-started.qmd#github-app) configured, the
required checks run on it like on any other PR.

## `main`

- **Require a pull request before merging.**
- **Require status checks to pass**: the job of
  [Require head branch](require-head-branch.qmd), so only `dev` can be
  merged.
- **Allow merge commits**: the [automatic merge](merge-pull-request.qmd)
  uses one.
- **Bypass list: your GitHub App.** The [release](package-release.qmd)
  pushes a version commit and a tag straight to `main`, which the
  pull-request rule would otherwise block.
- Block force pushes and deletion.

::: {.callout-important}
## Which token gets through
The release pushes with the App if configured, otherwise with the
`commit-push-pat` secret, otherwise with `GITHUB_TOKEN`:

- **GitHub App** — add it to the bypass list.
- **Personal access token** — users can't be added to the bypass list
  directly, but a PAT acts as its owner: it gets through if the owner has a
  role on the bypass list, e.g. *Repository admin*.
- **`GITHUB_TOKEN`** — can't bypass; the version commit is rejected on a
  protected `main`.
:::

## Status check names

A required status check is named after the **job** in your caller file,
combined with the job inside the reusable workflow — for example
`require-head-branch / verify-source-branch`. Pick the names from a PR's
checks list after the workflow has run once.
